Beacon Insurance and Meridian Retail Group represent contrasting customer success outcomes.

Beacon Insurance is a successful enterprise account: Q2 2026 was “highly successful,” with mature adoption and strong expansion potential [NL-025-S01]. Adoption exceeded benchmarks for KnowledgeHub (96.0%), TutorChat (92.2%), and CourseBuilder (80.4%), though InsightDash underperformed at 35.5% [NL-025-S03]. Beacon delivered measurable ROI: new adjuster onboarding fell from 6.2 weeks to 4.0 weeks, support escalations declined 22%, and verified queries reached 94% after the citation validation update [NL-025-S04]. It is now an expansion case, committing to the WorkflowCoach beta, adding 600 seats, and increasing ACV from $112,000 to $136,000 [NL-025-S06], with Q3 action items to support the expansion and December renewal [NL-025-S07].

Meridian Retail Group is a high-risk account requiring intervention: renewal probability is estimated at less than 40% without action [NL-026-S02]. Its core risk drivers are support ticket delays, permission-mapping friction in a decentralized store structure, and a missing Microsoft Teams integration that was informally suggested during sales [NL-026-S02]. Customer Success recommends against letting the account churn and proposes a pro-bono Enterprise Plan upgrade through October 15, 2026, a dedicated CSM, SCIM provisioning, and a discounted renewal path at $7,500/month for the first year [NL-026-S05].

In short, Beacon is a mature, expanding success story, while Meridian is an at-risk account being managed through a retention and stabilization plan.
